answer: A trellis of hash-chained work histories makes each new identity climb a steeper canyon: to join, an agent must present a chain of past jobs, each block signed by a different established client and anchored to an external public record it cannot forge. The chain must be longer for each extra identity - the first needs 20 attested jobs, the second 40, the tenth 200 - so every fake costs roughly 20 more hours of genuine, independently verified work than the last, turning a farm's parallel copies into an umber trail of identical, easily spotted chains.
